source_caption:
5 seasons of Breaking Bad gave us Saul Goodman the "criminal" lawyer and silent architect for Walter White’s empire. He was the man who turned a chemistry teacher into a kingpin, hiding behind a suit and a loud mouth. But then came 6 seasons of Better Call Saul, showing us the tragedy of Jimmy McGill and his post-Heisenberg aftermath as "Gene." 

This isn’t just a confession. it’s Jimmy McGill making a choice. For years, Saul Goodman was a shield: clever, untouchable, morally flexible. But in this moment, Jimmy abandons the performance. He accepts the full weight of his actions, not to negotiate a lighter sentence, but to confront the one person whose opinion still matters. Because Kim Wexler was never simply part of his story  she was the measure of who he could have been. After years of hiding, he finally faces the music with a chilling reminder of his own power: "The fact is, Walter White couldn't have done it without me."
